How to install it
  1. Download and extract the ZIP into a local folder.
  2. Ask your agent to verify the manifest and run the included installer.
  3. Start a new agent session so it can discover the installed skill.

Your first run is a conversation.
Keep a backup of important files. Read the audit and its limitations, then ask about any proposal you do not understand. Approve exact codes only after reviewing the plan.
Prepare your opening message


  
Control is part of the design.
The report informs your decision. It never grants permission to change files.
Review before execution
A fixed plan, explicit file IDs and a digest bind the supported operation.
Recovery has limits
Quarantine needs intact files and journals. Purge cannot be undone. Neither replaces your backup.
System changes need qualification
Tuning, repair and uninstall remain advice until a tested procedure exists. Untested environments stay unverified.
Keep private reports private
Reports can contain paths and machine details. Review an aggregate export before sharing; your agent provider has its own data boundary.


  
A little context goes a long way.

    
Why not delete every large folder?
A large folder may hold projects, application data or virtual disks. Measured size is evidence to review, not a promise of reclaimable space.

    
Will cleanup make my PC faster?
It depends on the bottleneck. Freeing storage does not remove CPU work from a running application. Syrin clean keeps performance advice separate from file cleanup.

    
Can I use this HTML offline?
Yes. Fonts, the sample report, both packages and prompt generation are embedded. Your agent or package installers may still need a network connection for their own work.
Download offline HTML

    
Which machines and agents are verified?
The support matrix separates implemented behavior from tested environments. A passing fixture test does not qualify every Windows version, device, filesystem or agent.
Read the support matrix

    
Read-only audit command
Use the verified extracted package with Windows PowerShell 5.1. This command collects metadata and writes a local report.
